violation_type.title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))
violation_type.short_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers
violation_type.typical_finding: During the walkthrough, an infant was observed sleeping with a bib on.     Note: The bib was removed immediately

finding_variants.text: During the walkthrough, an infant was observed sleeping with a bib on.     Note: The bib was removed immediately
An infant was observed with a pacifier attatched to her clothing by a cloth like string while asleep in the crib.     Note: The pacifier was removed during the inspection.
The operation did not check the bottles to make sure the label stayed on the bottle preventing the infant from choking.
There was a child in the infant room that had a bib on while sleeping in a crib. This is a choking hazard.    This was corrected at the time of the inspection by the Director removing the bib.
An infant was observed sleeping in a crib with a pacifier clip attached to the infant's sleep sack. This was corrected when the caregiver removed the pacifier clip from the crib.

The door separating the infant and preschool classrooms had a large gap beneath it. Preschool children were observed pushing small toys under the door into the infant room. An infant was observed retrieving one of the toys and was observed with the toy completely inside their mouth. The gap beneath the door allowed items to pass freely between classrooms, creating a potential choking hazard for infants.
